title: Eleven Miles of Open Ground
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：countryside　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 countryside 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 my uncle ① walked a countryside that no guidebook of his mentioned, and he said the walking was the whole of the holiday. The ② countryside, meaning the open ground and not the village, ran eleven miles and stayed that wide; countryside, he said, is the only thing in a holiday that is judged by how little of it is signposted.

Every ③ countryside in that county had the same hedgerow, and the ④ countryside at the end, meaning the one he kept for the last day and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever described twice. Countryside, my aunt said, is nine parts hedgerow and one part somebody willing to walk; my uncle said the walking is the part that fills eleven miles.

My grandmother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the countryside was the whole of the argument, meaning the people who live there and not the open ground. The ⑥ countryside, meaning the people and not any of that, is the only thing in an argument that everybody speaks for and nobody asks; countryside, she said, is either something you walk or the only word that means both an open ground and the people on it. He said the people are the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ countryside had become a line in a guidebook, and the guidebook had become an argument about the hedgerow. The ⑧ countryside of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in September, was one holiday and thirty years of walking; countryside, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to walk. She said the walking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ countryside I remember is the one at the end, which he walked in 1974 and is still described as the least signposted in the county. A ⑩ countryside, my aunt said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being walked; every countryside, she said, is a set of people that has agreed to look like an open ground. She said the people were the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 郊野（指那片开阔地带本身，与那个村子相对）
C. 固定搭配：walk a countryside 走一遍乡野
D. n. 乡村（指那个郡里每一片）
E. n. 乡村（指末尾那一片）
F. n. 乡下人；乡村居民（抽象：住在那里的居民）
G. n. 乡村（指旅行指南里提到的那一片）
H. n. 乡野；田园（抽象总称）

items.q: walked a countryside that no guidebook of his mentioned
The countryside, meaning the open ground and not the village
the countryside was the whole of the argument
the countryside had become a line in a guidebook
The countryside of the whole thing
A countryside, my aunt said in 1976

answers.why: walk a countryside 意为“走一遍乡野”，1960 年叔叔走了一遍他的任何旅行指南都没提到的乡野。
countryside 意为“郊野”，指那片开阔地带本身而不是那个村子，有十一英里宽。
countryside 指那个郡里每一片乡野，每一片都有同样的树篱。
countryside 指末尾那一片（他留给最后一天的那一片），是唯一有人描述过两次的。
countryside 意为“乡下人、乡村居民”，祖母说乡下人就是那场争论的全部，指的是住在那里的居民而不是那片开阔地带。
countryside 为转喻用法，指住在那里的居民而不是那片开阔地带，是争论里人人都替他们说话、却无人去问的东西。
countryside 意为“乡村”，指旅行指南里提到的那一片，到 1968 年这片乡野成了指南里的一行。
countryside 意为“乡野、田园”，叔叔九月写道，整件事的田园是一次假期三十年的行走。
countryside 意为“乡村、郊野”，我记得的是末尾那一片，他 1974 年走过，至今仍被说成全县路标最少的。
countryside 为抽象总称，姑姑说一片乡野是唯一会因为被走过而变好的东西。
